CHIEF COMPLAINT
Post-operative follow-up visit following bilateral reduction mammoplasty.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Pamela Cook is a 36-year-old female presenting for post-operative evaluation following bilateral reduction mammoplasty performed on 10-10-2020. Patient reports that her breasts are doing well. She notes that she previously had a lump noted under her left breast by PA Ruth Sanchez in March, which she has not felt since that time. Patient has been performing massages and using scar gel daily. She reports mild bothersome sensation related to one of the scars, particularly in the area of higher tension. Denies chills, fever, nausea, or vomiting. Reports resolution of back pain. Patient is otherwise doing well and enjoying summertime. Family is doing well.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Denies chills, fever, nausea, or vomiting. Denies current back pain. Denies hard spots, lumps, or bumps noted since last visit.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Bilateral reduction mammoplasty (10-10-2020)

MEDICATIONS
Mederma scar gel

ALLERGIES
Not documented

FAMILY HISTORY
Not documented

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient is enjoying summertime. Otherwise unremarkable.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Breasts: Bilateral incisions are well healed with no signs of infection or redness. One scar noted to have widened slightly. No lumps or abnormalities palpated. Overall healing is progressing well.

RESULTS
Photographs obtained for documentation and follow-up comparison.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Status post bilateral reduction mammoplasty with excellent healing and recovery.
2. Scar tissue formation with mild widening of one incision - continue Mederma scar gel twice daily and massage. Surgical revision (scar excision and re-closure) discussed but patient declines at this time. Will reassess in six months. Patient agrees to defer any revisions until at least one year post-operatively.
3. Follow-up appointment scheduled for six months to reassess scars and determine need for further intervention.
